payload.claim: The edit splices the new schema_version clause onto the existing defaults sentence with a semicolon instead of starting a new sentence, turning a compliant 20-word sentence (ending '...and `risk` `standard`.') into a 35-word run-on ('...and `risk` `standard`; `schema_version` absent or declared `1` reads as `1`, and any other declared value is refused.'). This is exactly the pattern CLAUDE.md's house style and the spec's own notes forbid ('no em-dash, semicolon, ... or a sentence over 25 words'); it merely escapes the `prose` gate because `in_scope()` in `.saffron/gates/prose.py` does not include `docs/agents/` in `INCLUDED_DIRS`, so the violation is never checked. The clause should be its own sentence, e.g. ending `standard`. `schema_version` absent or declared `1` reads as `1`; any other value is refused.` split further.
